sourceChecks.claim: Inspected Microsoft asynchronous acceptance/job identity/status and stored completion/error flow already checked live. Deferred acceptance differs from saved-result readiness and preserves later failure visibility.

Inspected RabbitMQ confirms documentation explicitly separating orthogonal publisher confirmations and consumer delivery acknowledgements. Neither acknowledges an external database transaction; retirement requires the relevant processing boundary.

Inspected AWS retry-safe APIs unique request identifiers and ACID token-plus-mutation requirement; RabbitMQ unacknowledged-delivery behavior. Durable atomic deduplication protects the specified database effect, not all external systems or message delivery.

Inspected Microsoft retry transient versus persistent errors, increasing delays, finite attempts and aggressive-retry overload; competing-consumer poison/dead-letter guidance. Isolation and deliberate duplicate-safe replay do not automatically repair failures.

Inspected competing-consumer ordering limitations and session/single-consumer grouping guidance. The supplied old/new trace demonstrates completion inversion; serialized per-entity effects through retries preserve dependency at a hot-key throughput cost.

Inspected queue-load-leveling producer-rate versus consumer-rate backlog, aggregate downstream bounds, finite quotas/retention and work shedding. Arithmetic 120-80=40 verified; workers cannot raise a saturated downstream limit by themselves.

Inspected Kafka design partition/group offsets, rewind, independently subscribed groups, retained/compacted log and external-output coordination limits. Offset progress does not delete history; retention and partition scope constrain replay/order.

Inspected Microsoft asynchronous pattern initial checks, acceptance and terminal status, plus queue operating complexity. Caller dependence justifies immediate authorization or delayed export rather than universal deferral.
